paper.title_en: Nucleon light-front transverse densities from three-body and quark + diquark Faddeev equations
paper.abstract_en: Nucleon elastic electromagnetic form factors obtained from two complementary continuum Schwinger function approaches -- a Poincaré-covariant three-body Faddeev equation formulated in rainbow-ladder truncation and a quark + fully-interacting-diquark, $q(qq)$, Faddeev equation -- are used to chart light-front transverse charge and magnetisation densities of the proton, the neutron, and their dressed valence quarks. Going beyond a comparison of observables, the bound-state amplitudes that underlie them are also compared. Both amplitudes are dominated by $s$-wave structures; and in the three-body solution, the mixed-antisymmetric (mixed-symmetric) flavour component is dominated by structures with the Dirac character of scalar (axialvector) diquark correlations, so that the association between these flavour components and diquark correlations is realised explicitly. The $q(qq)$ amplitude falls more slowly with the quark-diquark relative momentum than the three-body amplitude does with the corresponding Jacobi momentum. The two descriptions deliver mutually compatible densities, which match expectations based on modern parametrisations of data. Transverse-plane valence $u$- and $d$-quark Dirac radii are practically indistinguishable, whereas the $d$-quark Pauli radius is roughly 10% larger; and the valence $d$ quark is magnetically far more active than the valence $u$ quark, a feature tied to the mixed-symmetric (axialvector-diquark) components of the nucleon amplitude. For a $+\hat{x}$ polarised nucleon, positive charge is displaced in the $+\hat{y}$ direction, with the opposite effect for negative charge.
